subject: EU data residency & deployment mode 6 post-call follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Weber <l.weber@nordbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T13:15:00Z
Subject: EU data residency & deployment mode 6 post-call follow-up

Hi Lukas / Sofia -

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Production data must remain in the EU (data residency requirement for PII and audit logs).
- Low latency from EU-based apps (primary traffic from Frankfurt / eu-central).
- Regulatory team is likely to prefer dedicated tenancy or private VPC/on-prem for anything classified as sensitive.

High-level deployment options (tradeoffs)
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted, eu region): fastest to onboard (hours to days), lower operational overhead. We can guarantee that production workloads are served from an EU region (eu-west-1 / eu-central-1) with contractual residency terms, but please note hosted customers sometimes use cross-region fallback unless explicitly disabled by policy.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in EU): provides tenant isolation, predictable throughput, and we can disable automatic cross-region fallback for regulated customers. Lead time: typically 2-4 weeks depending on capacity.
3) Private (VPC or on-prem): full isolation and customer-managed network. Best for strict regulatory requirements but longer procurement and deployment lead times (4-12+ weeks depending on environment).

Ask / next steps
- Can you confirm whether the residency requirement covers logs/metrics and short-term KV cache, or only customer data/PII?
- I've attached our deployment options summary for your SOC/security team to review (redwood-deployment-options.pdf).
- If helpful, we can run a short pilot on Dedicated in eu-west-1 while we scope a Private deployment - would you be open to a 3-month pilot?
- Next call: technical deep-dive with Evelyn (solutions engineer) to cover network topology and encryption. I'm available next week Tuesday/Wednesday afternoon CEST.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (PDF)

From: Lukas Weber <l.weber@nordbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <s.martinez@nordbank.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: EU data residency & deployment mode 6 post-call follow-up

Thanks Marissa - helpful summary. A few clarifications from the compliance team: 

- Residency scope: We need all customer data and any derived data (embeddings, logs tied to request IDs) to remain in the EU. Short-term KV/cache where request-derived tokens might persist is included in the scope.
- Cross-region routing: our concern is any automatic failover that could route traffic through non-EU regions (even temporarily). Can this be fully disabled for production?
- Timeline: Procurement prefers a solution with minimal custom networking changes. Dedicated in eu-west-1 sounds like a good compromise if it guarantees no cross-region failover. What are the SLAs and lead time?

Can you also send SOC2 attestation / artifact we can include in our packet?

Best,
Lukas
Head of Cloud Platforms | NordBank
l.weber@nordbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-21T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: EU data residency & deployment mode 6 post-call follow-up

Hi Lukas -

Great questions - quick answers below and proposed concrete next steps: 

Answers
- Residency scope: Understood - we will treat embeddings, logs, and any derived artifacts as in-scope. For Hosted API we can contractually commit to EU-only processing and storage for production datasets; however, automatic cross-region fallback is enabled by default (for resilience). For regulated customers we offer an option to disable automatic cross-region fallback so data never leaves the selected region.
- Dedicated: We can provision dedicated GPU pools in eu-west-1 with tenant isolation and with automatic fallback disabled. Typical lead time: ~2-4 weeks after PO and network prep. SLA: we offer 99.9% uptime for Dedicated with response SLAs for incidents; I'll include the SLA doc in the follow-up pack.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full isolation and no cross-region routing. Lead time and cost are higher - this is usually chosen when the customer's compliance team requires customer-managed networking or air-gapped environments.

Attachments I'm sending now:
- SOC2-report-2025.pdf (attestation)
- redwood-deployment-options.pdf (overview)

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm scope (logs/embeddings included) so we can mark residency as required in our internal provisioning flow.
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Evelyn to review VPC peering, routing, and encryption (Evelyn is available Tue/Wed next week).
3) If you're open to a pilot, we'll provision a Dedicated pilot in eu-west-1 (3 months) while we scope Private. We'll send a draft mutual action plan (MAP) and a ballpark pricing figure for Dedicated.

If that sounds good I'll put the MAP + pricing draft together and loop Vivek on procurement questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: SOC2-report-2025.pdf (PDF); redwood-deployment-options.pdf (PDF)
